Which rows carry any spectral signal at all

Source: R/preprocess.R
has_spectral_coverage.Rd

The OSSL L0 tables have one row per soil LAYER, not per scan: a layer with no scan on a given instrument still gets a row, with every spectral column empty. That is 52.4% of the VisNIR table and 36.9% of MIR.

Usage

has_spectral_coverage(mask)

Arguments

mask

Integer/logical coverage matrix from mask_from_coverage()

Value

Logical vector, TRUE for rows with at least one covered band

Details

Such rows MUST be dropped before training. They cannot be caught downstream with is.finite(rowSums(X)), because the pipeline replaces non-finite cells with 0 first: an all-NA row becomes an all-zero row, passes is.finite(), and survives into training as a constant vector (constant -1 after SNV). Every such row is then identical to every other, so identical inputs force identical predictions and impose a hard, model-independent ceiling on R2 – which is why two unrelated algorithms previously landed within 0.05 of each other on every property.

Partial coverage is fine, and is precisely what the masked soilVAE exists to handle; only rows with no coverage at all are unusable.

A minimum-band threshold was considered and rejected on the data: coverage in OSSL v1.2 is perfectly bimodal. Every non-empty row has at least 1,051 of 1,076 VisNIR bands (the 1,051 floor is LUCAS/Metrohm starting at 400 nm rather than 350) or all 1,701 MIR bands. Nothing sits in between, so > 0 and >= 500 select exactly the same rows and a threshold would be arbitrary complexity. Re-check this if a future OSSL release mixes in instruments with genuinely sparse coverage.
